correctness.rationale: The quadrant chart is unit speed as a function of s=(3/2)sin²t, giving circumference 6. Independent uniform arclength coordinates give exactly ε/3 for S≤ε, a subset of D≤ε. On one quadrant, projecting its chord onto the mid-angle tangent direction gives D≥h cos(Δθ/2) with h the depth difference, hence h≤√2 ε and excess width at most a constant times ε times the squared increment of the tangent angle over a √2 ε interval. Integrating this squared increment gives O(ε) because the angle is monotone and has total variation π/2. Thus same-quadrant excess is O(ε²), despite cusp curvature divergence; nonadjacent quadrants have positive separation. For the two branches at one cusp, the exact vertical gap is c(a^(3/2)+b^(3/2)), so both depths are O(ε^(2/3)); the normal coordinate has derivative tending to −1, forcing |b−a|=O(ε). On a bounded support the change (a,b)=(ε^(2/3)u, ε^(2/3)u+εv) has Jacobian ε^(5/3), and the squared scaled chord converges to v²+4c²u³. For positive u the additional constraint a+b>ε is eventually automatic, equivalently losing at most ε²/2 per branch pair. Zero boundary area gives L¹ convergence of region indicators, and hence total variation after normalization. The limiting area is 2u_*/3 times B(1/3,3/2); multiplying by 8/36 gives the claimed coefficient, independently evaluated as 0.3533277500571 to the shown precision. Symmetry gives equiprobable cusp and ordered-orientation labels; the substitution w=(u/u_*)³ gives the Beta density and the normalized transverse coordinate is uniform conditional on w. The stated transformation concerns limiting coordinates; if applied at finite ε it can be defined arbitrarily off its real domain, where the conditional mass tends to zero. The uploaded numerical checker was inspected, not executed.
